sources.quote: He saw me so I went round to speak to him for a few minutes. He told me that he and Foster Harter had been fishing in Donegal and that he was going to fish South now. … He (Todd) looked awfully nervous and uncomfortable. I thought of Mark.
sources.context: Wilde to William Ward, Sunday [6 August 1876] (MS Magdalen). What Wilde did on seeing them: he went round to the box and made conversation, and Todd talked about fishing. The elision drops the judgement, which is quoted in full on the connection.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: Wilde's own conduct on the night - he went over, and he noticed the discomfort.

name: Charles John Todd
bio: A Magdalen undergraduate of Wilde's own years (1874-7) who took orders and served as Chaplain to the Royal Navy from 1881 to 1909, dying at eighty-five. He is on this map for one evening in Dublin in the summer of 1876, when Wilde walked into a theatre at ten o'clock and found him sitting at the back of a private box with a Magdalen chorister. Wilde wrote about it to William Ward, decided in Todd's favour, and asked Ward to tell nobody.
bio_note: The only evidence is Wilde's letter. His later life is from the editors' note and nothing in it is connected to this evening.
